data.stem: Lord Ripon's 1882 Resolution is hailed as the Magna Carta of which field?
data.explanation: Local self-government is correct: Ripon's 1882 Resolution is called the Magna Carta of local self-government, and he is regarded as its father in India. Financial decentralisation is the theme of Lord Mayo's 1870 Resolution, provincial autonomy came with the 1935 Act, and public service recruitment was not the Resolution's theme, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: In which year did the first municipal corporation in India come into existence, at Madras?
data.explanation: 1688 is correct: the Madras corporation came into existence on 29 September 1688, although its charter was issued in December 1687. The year 1687 is only the charter date, 1726 is when Bombay and Calcutta received corporations, and 1882 is the year of Ripon's Resolution, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Under which Act was local self-government declared a provincial subject?
data.explanation: The Government of India Act, 1935 is correct, since it made local self-government a provincial subject under provincial autonomy. The 1919 Act had made it a transferred subject in the provinces, the Cantonments Act of 1924 was a separate central statute, and the Indian Councils Act of 1909 dealt with legislative councils, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which government's bill to give municipal bodies constitutional status was defeated in the Rajya Sabha in October 1989?
data.explanation: The Rajiv Gandhi government is correct: its 65th Amendment (Nagarpalika) Bill passed the Lok Sabha but was defeated in the Rajya Sabha in October 1989. The V. P. Singh government's revised bill lapsed on dissolution, the Narasimha Rao government's bill became the 74th Amendment, and Indira Gandhi's government had ended in 1984, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about Part IX-A added by the 74th Amendment:
1. It covers Articles 243P to 243ZG.
2. It adds a Twelfth Schedule listing eighteen functions of municipalities.
3. It applies automatically to scheduled and tribal areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 1 and 2 only is correct: Part IX-A covers Articles 243P to 243ZG, and the Twelfth Schedule lists eighteen municipal functions. Statement 3 is wrong because the Part does not apply to scheduled and tribal areas unless Parliament extends it, so every option that includes statement 3 is incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which kind of municipality is set up for an area in transition from rural to urban status?
data.explanation: A nagar panchayat is correct: the 74th Amendment provides it for a transitional area, meaning one moving from rural to urban character. A municipal council serves a smaller urban area, a municipal corporation serves a larger one, and a town area committee is a separate state-created body, so those three are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Where an industrial establishment provides municipal services in an area, what may the Governor specify?
options: An industrial township with no municipality
data.explanation: An industrial township with no municipality is correct, because the Governor may specify such an area and then no municipality is constituted there. A metropolitan area gets a planning committee, a cantonment area is governed by a cantonment board, and a scheduled area lies outside the Part, so those three options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: What is the usual term of a mayor in a municipal corporation in most states?
data.explanation: A one-year renewable term is correct: in most states the mayor is elected for one year and may be renewed, and the office is largely ceremonial. Five years is the term of the municipality itself, while a two-year non-renewable term and an open-ended tenure are not the standard arrangement, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which feature sets a notified area committee apart from a municipality?
options: It has a mayor as its head
It is set up by the Union Government
It is entirely nominated, including its chairman
It is created by a state legislature act
data.explanation: Entire nomination, including the chairman, is correct. A notified area committee is created by a gazette notification rather than a statute, and it has no mayor. The Union Government does not set it up, since state governments do, and it is not created by an act of the state legislature, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: A cantonment area has a civil population of 12,000. Under the classification of cantonment boards, which category applies?
data.explanation: Category II is correct: the categories are above 50,000 (I), 10,000 to 50,000 (II), 2,500 to 10,000 (III) and below 2,500 (IV), so a population of 12,000 falls in II. Categories I, III and IV cover different population bands, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: At what population must a wards committee be constituted within a municipality?
data.explanation: Three lakh or more is correct, since the 74th Amendment requires a wards committee in a municipality of that population. Thresholds of one or five lakh do not trigger the requirement, and ten lakh is the figure used to define a metropolitan area for planning, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: What minimum share of the seats in a municipality must be reserved for women?
data.explanation: One-third is correct: not less than one-third of all seats must go to women, and that total includes seats for SC and ST women. One-fourth, one-half and one-fifth are not the statutory minimum, so those options are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Within how long after a municipality's dissolution must fresh elections be completed?
data.explanation: Six months is correct: fresh elections must be completed before six months from the date of dissolution expire. Three months, one year and two years are not the period the Act sets, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: A municipality is dissolved with four months of its five-year term still to run. What does the Act require?
options: A fresh full five-year term needs an election within six months
The reconstituted body serves a full five-year term
No fresh election is required for the short remainder
The state must hold elections within one year
data.explanation: No fresh election is required for the short remainder is correct: where the balance of the term is less than six months, no election is needed for that period. A reconstituted body serves only the balance of the original term, not a full five years, so the other options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which body is vested with superintendence of municipal electoral rolls and the conduct of municipal elections?
data.explanation: The State Election Commission is correct, because the 74th Amendment vests superintendence, direction and control of municipal electoral rolls and elections in it. The Election Commission of India conducts Parliament and assembly polls, the District Magistrate and the Municipal Commissioner do not hold this function, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following on municipal finance:
1. The state legislature may authorise a municipality to levy taxes, duties, tolls and fees.
2. The Governor places the state finance commission's recommendations, with an action-taken report, before the state legislature.
3. Municipalities may borrow from financial institutions without any state approval.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 1 and 2 only is correct. Statement 3 is wrong because municipal borrowing from financial institutions needs the state government's approval, so every option containing statement 3 is incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: What population must a metropolitan area have before a metropolitan planning committee is required?
data.explanation: Ten lakh or more is correct: a metropolitan area has a population of ten lakh or more across one or more districts and comprises two or more municipalities, panchayats or contiguous areas. Three lakh is the wards committee threshold, while five lakh and one crore do not define the metropolitan area, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Under which Article is the committee for district planning provided?
data.explanation: Article 243ZD is correct for the district planning committee. Article 243ZE covers the metropolitan planning committee, Article 243W deals with the powers and functions of municipalities, and Article 243Y covers the finance commission, so those three options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: In which year was the Central Council of Local Government set up under Article 263?
data.explanation: 1954 is correct: the Council was set up that year by a presidential order under Article 263. 1924 is the year of the earlier Cantonments Act, 1958 is when the Council stopped covering rural bodies, and 1989 is when the Nagarpalika Bill was introduced, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Under which arrangement do municipal staff become members of the state services and move into state departments?
data.explanation: The integrated personnel system is correct, because state and local staff form one service and can move between local bodies and state departments. The separate system keeps staff within one local body, the unified system uses state cadres that move only among local bodies, and a decentralised system is not one of the three recognised arrangements, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which of these is NOT a source of revenue for urban local bodies?
options: Income tax collected by the Union
data.explanation: Income tax collected by the Union is the NOT answer, since it is not among the five sources of urban local income. Property tax is part of tax revenue, devolution from the state is a recognised source, and water user charges belong to non-tax revenue, so the other three options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: A candidate aged 22 wants to stand for a municipal seat. Which statement about disqualification is correct?
options: The age bar of 25 applies, so the candidate is disqualified
The candidate is not disqualified merely for being under 25
data.explanation: The candidate is not disqualified merely for being under 25 is correct, because a person who has reached 21 cannot be disqualified on the ground of being less than 25. The 30-year minimum and the 25-year bar are not the rules described, and a 21-year-old may stand, so those options are wrong.
data.label: practice
